title: Billing log provenance and access policy for compliance-facing customers
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Define and implement a tamper-evident provenance and access-control policy for all billing and metering logs used in customer invoicing, quota enforcement, and usage reconciliation. This ticket captures the engineering design and implementation tasks to ensure logs are cryptographically verifiable, retention meets regulatory / SOC expectations, and access is tightly controlled and auditable.

Scope:
- All usage events that contribute to billing units (token counts, embedding units, request/response metadata, quota/limit adjustments)
- Rate-limit and quota decision logs (overrides, emergency bypass, admin changes)
- Aggregation outputs used for invoices and downstream billing pipelines

Non-goals:
- Rewriting the existing billing pipeline for performance (only minimal adapters to emit provenance metadata)
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end hashed append-only log for billing events with daily Merkle root published to internal key-value store and archived copies
RBAC enforced via IAM roles: billing-read, billing-reconcile, billing-admin with least privilege; all access recorded and exported to SIEM
Retention policy documented and automated: hot storage 90 days, warm 2 years, cold archive 7 years (customer-selectable up to 7 years)
Signed snapshots and tamper-evidence proofs available for SOC2 auditors on request with minimal operator effort
Rate-limit/quota-change events include user, timestamp, justification, ticket link, and are immutable once written to the append-only stream
steps: Design ledger format: event envelope with sequence_id, timestamp, event_type, payload_hash, prev_hash, signature_metadata
Implement append-only writer as sidecar in the metering ingestion pipeline; write to S3-backed immutable archive and streaming buffer for near-term queries
Create daily Merkle root generator job; store root in KMS-backed secrets store and push to internal ledger index for easy retrieval
Enforce RBAC on both runtime exposure (APIs) and storage access using cloud IAM and VPC restrictions; integrate with Okta groups for billing roles
Add audit-export hook to forward access events to SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) with retention aligned to compliance requirements
Provide reconciliation tooling: a lightweight verifier that replays archived events and recomputes aggregates used on invoices
Document retention/erasure controls and data residency options for customers in Confluence and update customer-facing policy doc
comments: 2026-01-16 Maya Chen: Initial draft of the ledger schema attached to Confluence. Opted for Merkle roots instead of solely HMAC because auditors requested public verifiability of snapshot integrity without exposing HMAC keys.
2026-01-22 Rajat Patel: Implemented sidecar prototype that emits sequence_id and prev_hash. Local tests show negligible write latency (~2ms additional per batch) when batched by 100 events.

2026-01-29 Security review (A. Gomez): Recommended rotating signing keys quarterly and storing snapshot anchors in a KMS-backed SIEM index; also flagged emergency break-glass access as needing additional audit hooks.
2026-02-03 PM review (L. Ortega): Added requirement to include ticket links for manual quota overrides so finance can trace the business justification for adjustments.
2026-02-08 Operations (S. Nguyen): Noted that cold archive retrieval for auditors may take up to 24-48 hours depending on region; propose pre-warm window for audit requests to ensure timely access.
2026-02-10 Rajat Patel: Broke down implementation into three PRs: writer, merkle job, verifier. Opening PRs this week; coordinating with infra for encryption-at-rest policy enforcement.
notes: Design trade-offs: Use append-only S3 with object-lock + server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) for archive immutability. Supplement with signed Merkle roots to allow short-term validators to verify integrity without key access. Avoid blockchain or external ledger dependencies to keep cost and complexity low.
runbook_summary: For auditor requests: 1) Request ID and time window 2) Trigger pre-warm for cold archive if older than 90 days 3) Generate signed Merkle proof bundle + verifier script and deliver over secure transfer. Record request in 'billing-audit-requests' docket.
mitigations: Key rotation, least-privilege IAM, SIEM alerting on high-volume export requests, periodic integrity sweeps, and regression tests for reconciliation tooling.
